correctness.rationale: Independent parent choices and the uniform ancestor probability give an exact single-attachment covariance for each t. Summation and a verified telescoping decrement produce the cross-moment matrix, including zero cases \(i\ge j\) and \(i=1,j=2\). Reciprocal-square positivity establishes a unique crossover, and Euler–Maclaurin with stated remainder gives \(J_i=2i^2-2i/3+O(1)\). Exhaustive exact-rational enumeration over 46,233 recursive trees confirms finite instances; it is supporting evidence, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A single algebraic inverse-square decrement common to every source label and a quadratic-age crossover form a motivated finite-sample dependence law for two fundamental random-tree observables. The sign reversal and exact birth horizon are invisible in individual marginal moments and ordinary normalized asymptotic independence. They provide concrete information for studying age-related dependencies in recursive network models; no broader theorem is asserted.
